experiment_name: MonopolyZero strength pilot: paired evaluation, pre-training baseline vs. 32-game trained checkpoint

algorithm_config.seat_rotation: 4 seats x 5 seeds = 20 games per checkpoint

metrics.wilson_interval_overlap: baseline [0.0, 0.161] and trained [0.009, 0.236] overlap almost completely; trained's interval is not entirely above baseline's, so the non-overlap test fails

result: NO-SIGNAL. Trained checkpoint won 1/20 vs. baseline's 0/20, and mean net worth was nominally higher (3759.3 vs 2450.4), but the Wilson 95% intervals overlap almost completely ([0%, 16.1%] vs [0.9%, 23.6%]) - not a statistically supported improvement at this sample size (20 games/checkpoint). Both checkpoints: 0 illegal actions, 0 crashes, asu_modules_loaded count 0 (ASU never touched, ASU benchmark not run per task instruction). Fixed-agent fallbacks: 17 per checkpoint (34 total) - baseline's came from fixed-b/fixed-c, trained's all from fixed-c; both are the documented compatibility-fallback path, not errors. Round-cap rate rose from 45% to 55% (trained games more often ran the full 200 rounds) - descriptive only, not itself evidence of strength either way.
notes: model_checkpoint is null at top level because this entry compares two checkpoints, not one - both are under metrics.baseline/metrics.trained. Per-seed/per-seat results (40 individual games: seed, focus_seat, winner, rounds, decisions, net_worth) are in the raw stdout log's per_game arrays, not duplicated here. code_commit_sha is the commit that had both checkpoints already trained and committed-to-log (013's commit) - the clean HEAD this eval actually ran against.
